description: Paper-level train/validation/test split over the 50-paper corpus, stratified by topic. Papers are matched by the title fragments below, which are checked for uniqueness at load time.

rationale.why_by_paper: Splitting by chunk would put passages from the same paper on both sides, so a model could score well by memorising a paper's vocabulary. Only a paper-level split measures transfer to unseen documents.
rationale.why_three_way: The Phase 3 re-ranker study had no validation split and selected a learning rate by looking at the held-out set, which biases that number. Validation exists so test is touched once, at the end.
rationale.why_stratified: The dominant error mode measured in Phase 2 is cross-paper contamination, which only appears when a corpus contains papers that are genuinely hard to tell apart. Every topic cluster therefore appears in all three splits: the test split contains papers whose near-neighbours the model trained on.
